comparator.sourceNotes: The dated study guide lists 60 EC per year. This example uses the first two listed thematic courses available in the indicated second semester, and the first listed third-year deepening module. The 30 EC free elective space remains open. The first-year Dutch writing diagnostic carries no credit and is recorded in the notes.

core: Sociological theory, social structures, inequality and social change
Political science, governance and collective responses to social problems
Psychology of individual and group behaviour in society
Cultural anthropology and socio-spatial inquiry as distinct UvA core fields, with acknowledged UCR coverage limits
Qualitative and quantitative social research and integrated independent inquiry
adjacent: Inequality, inclusion, rights and policy responses
Health and society as an official second-year thematic direction
Sustainability, conflict and international social challenges
questions: How do individual behaviour and social structures jointly shape inequality and change?
How can research inform public and civic responses to complex social problems?
How do social environments and institutions shape health and wellbeing?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Uses markets, incentives and macroeconomic indicators to explain how policy problems arise and who is affected.
Studies public goods, taxation, redistribution and expenditure on health, education and social insurance.
Uses regression and causal estimation to evaluate evidence on economic and social policy.
Uses sampling, measurement, surveys, experimental reasoning and introductory inference in an empirical project.
Studies inclusion and psychological safety in organisations and conducts a quantitative survey about leadership and belonging.
Develops prediction and classification and checks performance on new data, supporting evaluation of population and behavioural datasets.
Uses place-based cases to examine the relationships among water risk, infrastructure, local communities, institutions and justice.
Uses concepts of justice, institutions and participation to assess sustainability decisions and develop policy advice for a Zeeland issue.
Compares legal institutions and examines links between justice, race, gender and social change.
Uses primary sources and oral history to investigate gender, sexuality and social exclusion.
Evaluates legal and philosophical accounts of rights and studies protections through international institutions and cases.
Compares institutions, rights and remedies, including the scope for public participation and procedural fairness.
Studies EU legal institutions, competences, citizenship and remedies to understand how policy acquires legal effect.
Uses moral theories and argument to assess responsibilities, rights and the fairness of collective decisions.
Examines how emotions shape judgement, relationships and action, complementing the study of behaviour and wellbeing.
Examines authority, rights, equality and democracy through political thought.
Compares institutions, parties, participation and democratic change using cases and political data.
Studies EU policymaking and tests explanations of legislative behaviour in an empirical project.
Uses national and international cases to compare policymaking stages and develop policy memos.
Studies conflict, inequality, identity and peacebuilding and develops a policy brief grounded in research.
Uses sociological theory to interpret inequality, group boundaries, social structure and migration.
Designs and conducts qualitative research using interviews, focus groups, observation and thematic interpretation.
Uses modern and critical social theory to interpret social action, institutions and exclusion.
Examines social movements and environmental justice through cases and feminist and anticolonial perspectives.
Uses social theory and research to investigate civil society, social trust and mobilisation.
Analyses population health, determinants, evidence and potential interventions through an applied local research project.
Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour, learning and social influence.
Studies group processes, social influence, prejudice and how people form judgements about others.
Selects and evaluates statistical models for behavioural questions and examines experimental design.
Studies health inequalities, behaviour, prevention and illness in social and cultural contexts.
Uses interviews, psychological assessment and case work to study how mental-health services understand needs and plan support.
Uses systematic search, evidence appraisal and meta-analysis to synthesise research.
Studies development and social contexts across life stages and analyses a life-story interview.
Uses social and behavioural research to design educational resources on belonging, resilience and prevention.
Uses media and historical evidence to examine racial representation, power, exclusion and resistance.

alternatives.label: Social science, behaviour and public challenges
alternatives.concept: Study social problems through sociology, psychology, politics and research. Use empirical evidence to examine inequality, sustainability and how institutions respond.
alternatives.labelReason: Sociology, psychology, politics and research form the core, with applications in sustainability and civic life.
progression: Economics and social foundations start in the first term. Research methods precede public economics, and psychology precedes advanced evidence synthesis and health psychology. Current offerings and formal prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Inequality, rights and public policy
alternatives.concept: Study how institutions, rights and public policy shape inequality. Combine sociology and political research with gender history, constitutional law and public economics.
alternatives.labelReason: Rights, institutions, redistribution and histories of exclusion shape the selection.
alternatives.distinctness: 6 courses (45 EC) differ in each direction from the broad option. Law, rights, gender and political institutions distinguish the focus.
progression: The law and economics foundations precede constitutional and EU law and public economics. Current offerings and formal prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Health, behaviour and social policy
alternatives.concept: Study how behaviour, social conditions and public policy affect health. Combine epidemiology and health psychology with evidence synthesis, public economics and policy analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: Population health, behaviour, inequality and the evaluation of policy shape the selection.
alternatives.distinctness: 6 courses differ from the broad option and 11 from the inequality option in each direction. The choices concentrate on population health, behaviour, evidence synthesis and policy.
progression: Brain & Behavior and research methods precede clinical and health psychology and systematic review. Statistical analysis supports later evidence synthesis and econometrics. Current offerings and formal prerequisites pass.

selection.assessment: Three distinct programmes address broad social research, institutional inequality, and the social and behavioural determinants of health. All pass the pairwise distinctness and feasibility checks.

blocks: Both study gender, sexuality and power. UCR uses North American historical sources and oral histories.
Both introduce sociological explanations of inequality, cohesion and culture.
Both conduct a qualitative project from research question to data collection and interpretation.
Both use social theory to explain relationships between action and social structures. UvA integrates several social-science disciplines.
Both study group influence, attitudes and behaviour. UvA also introduces cognition, learning and motivation.
Both select statistical methods, analyse data and interpret results. UCR uses behavioural datasets and UvA develops a broader social-science research project.
Both plan a systematic literature search, select and appraise evidence, and synthesise findings. UCR uses meta-analysis, while UvA integrates perspectives across social-science disciplines.
Both introduce political science through comparative study of institutions, actors and participation.
Both study the causes of conflict and compare approaches to peacebuilding across disciplines.
Both study policy formation, decisions, implementation and evaluation. UvA adds a group investigation of an applied policy problem.
Both develop academic reading, writing and reflection. UvA teaches these in a short tutored practicum.
Both teach study design, data collection and basic analysis. UvA also studies social research traditions and qualitative methods.
Both apply sustainability analysis to a specific problem and consider practical responses. UvA works in teams on a case from an external client.

notes.text: UvA combines sociology, psychology, political science, anthropology and human geography in one degree. UCR offers related social science and research, while UvA provides dedicated anthropology and urban geography courses and a required sequence of integration practica.

audience.programmeDescription: Interdisciplinary Social Science at the University of Amsterdam brings five social sciences together to investigate problems such as inequality and sustainability. Students learn qualitative and quantitative methods, apply them in projects and complete an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options focus on broad social research, inequality and public policy, or the social and behavioural determinants of health. UvA combines these kinds of questions with dedicated anthropology, human geography and interdisciplinary fieldwork.
